subject.title: Reject unsupported diagnostics OTel grpc config

question: Should OpenClaw retire the shipped `diagnostics.otel.protocol = "grpc"` config value through this doctor migration now, or keep accepting it until real gRPC export exists?
rationale: The patch is code-correct, but it narrows a shipped config contract and can disable telemetry during doctor repair; automation cannot choose that compatibility policy for maintainers.

options.title: Accept reject-plus-doctor path
options.body: Land this PR after accepting that legacy `grpc` configs are migrated away and enabled OTLP telemetry may be disabled until users configure HTTP/protobuf export.

options.title: Require real gRPC support
options.body: Pause or close this PR and sponsor a larger exporter implementation with gRPC dependencies, runtime support, docs, and live/protocol tests.

options.title: Keep warning-only compatibility
options.body: Reject the schema narrowing and keep accepting `grpc` as a config value while relying on the runtime unsupported-protocol warning.

recommendation.title: Accept reject-plus-doctor path
recommendation.body: Land this PR after accepting that legacy `grpc` configs are migrated away and enabled OTLP telemetry may be disabled until users configure HTTP/protobuf export.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the diagnostics exporter/config surface and are the strongest history-backed owner for the compatibility direction.
